articleText:
[Hacker News — kernel.dev]
Why is Gemini 4 Carbon taking so long? November 2026 While benchmarking Gemini 4 Carbon on one of our private evals, we found something surprising: it spent close to an hour completing tasks that routinely took Opus and Astra only a few minutes: Time and cost per trial Left is faster; lower is cheaper. API list price On a $200 plan, fully used Carbon is priced at its post-introductory rate. Subscription subsidization rates used: Opus 40×, Astra 13×, Carbon 3×, Hydrogen 17×. Turns out we weren't alone in noticing this. Theo - t3.gg @theo I don't really know how to properly emphasize this. Gemini 4 Carbon is unacceptably slow in real world usage. Gemini 4 Carbon low: 22m21s Opus 5.5 high: 9m33s Nov 11, 2026 828 104 replies
reactions: [Hacker News] It’s unlikely to be deliberate tbh, it’s more likely the data, algorithms and the training environments aren’t quite as good as Anthropic, Open AI is a lot closer to Google than people want to admit.
[Hacker News] I'd guess that it's because Google eats its own dogfood, and if they didn't train the models to be overly meticulous, the existing codebase would implode under a tsunami of slop.

[Hacker News] Then that's "test-time scaling" again and Google then showed that they can reach frontier level benchmark results using it. It's pretty cool as a technology actually (the demonstrated capability), even if the model is not so useful when it's slow.
[Hacker News] yeah i tried using it its not efficient at all. just burns up the token and not get the work done.

items.title: Why is Gemini 4 Carbon taking so long?
